q-34071.name: Question 1
q-34071.problem: Find the shortest distance between the point $P(1,1,-1)$ and the plane $Π$ with equation $(r-⟨3,0,1⟩)\cdot ⟨1,-8,4⟩=0.$
q-34071.worked_solution:
Let's pick a point on the plane, for instance, $Q(3,0,1).$ Then 

$$
\begin{aligned}\overset{\to }{PQ} & =⟨3,0,1⟩-⟨1,1,-1⟩ \\  & =⟨2,-1,2⟩.\end{aligned}
$$

Also, from the equation of the plane, we get a normal vector $n=⟨1,-8,4⟩.$

Finally, the shortest distance from the point $P$ to the plane $Π$ is the absolute value of the scalar projection of $\overset{\to }{PQ}$ onto the normal vector of the plane:

$$
\begin{aligned}d & =|{\text{comp}}_{n}\,\overset{\to }{PQ}| \\  & =\frac{|\overset{\to }{PQ}\cdot n|}{|n|} \\  & =\frac{|2\cdot 1+(-1)\cdot (-8)+2\cdot 4|}{\sqrt{{1}^{2}+(-8)^{2}+{4}^{2}}} \\  & =\frac{|2+8+8|}{\sqrt{1+64+16}} \\  & =\frac{|18|}{\sqrt{81}} \\  & =2\end{aligned}
$$

q-129100.problem: Find the shortest distance between the point $P(8,-3,5)$ and the plane $Π$ with equation $(r-⟨7,-2,4⟩)\cdot ⟨-2,-3,6⟩=0.$
q-129100.worked_solution:
Let's pick a point on the plane, for instance, $Q(7,-2,4).$ Then

$$
\begin{aligned}\overset{\to }{PQ} & =⟨7,-2,4⟩-⟨8,-3,5⟩ \\  & =⟨-1,1,-1⟩.\end{aligned}
$$

Also, from the equation of the plane, we get a normal vector $n=⟨-2,-3,6⟩.$

Finally, the shortest distance from the point $P$ to the plane $Π$ is the absolute value of the scalar projection of $\overset{\to }{PQ}$ onto the normal vector of the plane:

$$
\begin{aligned}d & =|{\text{comp}}_{n}\,\overset{\to }{PQ}| \\  & =\frac{|\overset{\to }{PQ}\cdot n|}{|n|} \\  & =\frac{|(-1)\cdot (-2)+1\cdot (-3)+(-1)\cdot 6|}{\sqrt{(-2)^{2}+(-3)^{2}+{6}^{2}}} \\  & =\frac{|2-3-6|}{\sqrt{4+9+36}} \\  & =\frac{|-7|}{\sqrt{49}} \\  & =\frac{7}{7} \\  & =1.\end{aligned}
$$

q-129142.worked_solution:

$$
\begin{aligned}⟨x,y,z⟩\cdot ⟨-2,4,4⟩ & =8 \\ -2x+4y+4z & =8 \\ 4z & =8+2x-4y \\ z & =2+\frac{x}{2}-y.\end{aligned}
$$

Setting $x=2$ and $y=1,$ we get 

$$
z=2+\frac{2}{2}-1=2.

$$
\begin{aligned}\overset{\to }{PQ} & =⟨2,1,2⟩-⟨-3,2,6⟩ \\  & =⟨5,-1,-4⟩.\end{aligned}
$$

Find the shortest distance between the point P(−1,0,2) and the plane Π with equation 2x−y+2z=−1.

EXPLANATION

Let's start by picking a point on the plane. To do that, we simply substitute some concrete values for x and y into the equation and solve for z. Let's choose x=2 and y=3 (though it doesn't really matter what values we choose). Solving for z, we get

2x−y+2z=−12(2)−(3)+2z=−12z=−2z=−1.

So, we get the point Q(2,3,−1) which lies on the plane.

Computing PQ→, we get

PQ→=⟨2,3,−1⟩−⟨−1,0,2⟩=⟨3,3,−3⟩.

We also need a normal vector to the plane. For any Cartesian equation of a plane ax+by+cz=d, the normal vector is n=⟨a,b,c⟩. So, for the plane Π, we have n=⟨2,−1,2⟩.

Finally, the shortest distance from the point P to the plane Π is the absolute value of the scalar projection of PQ→ onto the normal vector of the plane:

d=|compnPQ→|=|PQ→⋅n||n|=|3⋅2+3⋅(−1)+(−3)⋅2|22+(−1)2+22=|6−3−6|4+1+4=|−3|9=1
